FOLLOWING:
 WP(C) NO. 15860 OF 2016 2 Sindhu Preman vs The District Collector, Ernakulam on 12 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101658728/
1  JUDGMENT Dated this the 12th day of April, 2024 This writ petition was filed in the year 2016 seeking the following reliefs:
"i) Call for the records relating to Exts.P1 to P7 from the respondents;
ii) Quash Exts.P5 and P6 revenue recovery notices by a writ of certiorai or any other writ, order or direction;
iii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other writ, order or direction to the 4th respondent to regularize the margin money loan and grant installment facility to clear the loan arrears:
iv) Such other relief's which is deemed to be fit and proper to this honourable court in the facts and circumstances of the case."
2. When this writ petition was admitted on 26.4.2016, an interim order was granted on condition that the petitioner deposits Rs.40,000/- within a period of one month. 
3. The learned counsel for the petitioner seeks further time to get instructions. However,
considering the limited nature of the reliefs sought and the facts and circumstances of the case, I am inclined to dispose of the writ petition permitting the petitioner to pay off the present arrears in 12 equal monthly instalments commencing from 30.5.2024. The subsequent instalments shall be paid on or before the last working day of the succeeding months. The petitioner shall approach the 4th respondent with a copy of this judgment and the 4 th respondent shall intimate the petitioner of the liability payable by the petitioner as on today. 
Considering the fact that the writ petition has been pending before this Court from 2016 onwards and since the petitioner has got considerable opportunity to settle the liability, no further extension of time will be granted under any circumstances. If the petitioner does not clear the liability as aforesaid, the recovery proceedings against her may continue. 
Sd/-
